business_flow: User interacts with an e-commerce-like application. Actions include viewing/creating/updating addresses, basket items, cards, feedbacks, complaints, deliveries, products, recycles, security Q/A, users, images/assets, captcha, chatbot, wallet and socket interactions. Multiple REST and /rest endpoints exist for cart checkout, coupons, checkout, product reviews, user management, wallets and admin functions. Requests contain bearer tokens and cookies. Several endpoints accept IDs in path or parameters and some accept client-modifiable fields (quantity, paymentId, balance, coupon codes).
thought_process: I will inspect each HAR entry and apply the five checks (IDOR BLA9, State Manipulation BLA3, Sequence Bypass BLA6, Shadow Endpoints BLA10, Internal Disclosure BLA8).
Report one finding per vulnerable endpoint/interaction. Only actual observed requests/responses are considered.
For every finding include reproduction_guide with payload_mutation and a curl_command using placeholders {{auth_token}} and {{target_id}} when applicable.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: GET /api/Addresss/{id} (Entry #5) returns address data for ID 7 using a direct object reference. The request uses a bearer token but responses indicate different user contexts in other entries; ownership enforcement is not shown. This is an IDOR candidate because addresses are accessed by numeric ID in path and PUT/DELETE operations for Addresss/7 exist (Entry #6).

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Change path ID from your address id (e.g., 7) to another user's address id (e.g., 1 or {{target_id}}) to attempt access.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: POST /api/BasketItems/ (Entry #9 and #10) accepts BasketId and quantity in request body. BasketId is provided by client as string '6' and ProductId is set by client; quantity is modifiable. Client can set BasketId to arbitrary value or change quantity to manipulate order total/fulfillment. This indicates modifiable critical fields (state manipulation).

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Change 'BasketId' from "6" to another basket ID (e.g., "{{target_id}}") or set 'quantity' to a large value (e.g., 1000).

potential_vulnerabilities.description: DELETE /api/BasketItems/9 (Entry #11) deletes a basket item by numeric ID in path. Existence of GET/PUT/DELETE for BasketItems/9 shows direct object reference without demonstrated ownership checks — an IDOR candidate.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Change path ID from 9 to another item id ({{target_id}}) to attempt deletion of another user's basket item.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: PUT /api/BasketItems/9 (Entry #13) accepts 'quantity' in body and updates item quantity. Critical order parameter modifiable by client; allows inflating or deflating quantities impacting pricing/stock.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Change 'quantity' from 1 to 0 or 1000 to test modification of order quantity.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: GET /api/Cards/{id} (Entry #16) returns card details for ID 7. Cards endpoints accept direct ID in path and POST to create cards exists (Entry #15). Card retrieval by ID suggests possible IDOR if insufficient ownership checks.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Change path ID from 7 to another card id ({{target_id}}) to attempt access to other user's card details.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: Multiple API responses (Entry #3 cookie and authorization JWT) reveal internal user data and internal IDs in JWT payload such as 'id':23, internal tokens, topSecret/totpSecret fields. Internal IDs and secrets disclosed in cookies/Authorization header content indicate internal disclosure.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: No request mutation needed — inspect Authorization token or cookie values returned in requests/responses to extract internal fields.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: POST /api/Recycles/ (Entry #36) accepts 'UserId', 'AddressId', and 'quantity' in request body. Client-supplied UserId and AddressId allow forging requests on behalf of other users (state manipulation / broken authorization).

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Change 'UserId' from 23 to another user's id (e.g., {{target_id}}) or change 'quantity' to an inflated value.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: POST /api/Complaints/ (Entry #21) accepts 'UserId' in body. Client can submit complaints under arbitrary UserId, indicating potential IDOR/authorization bypass if server does not validate that UserId belongs to the authenticated principal.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Change 'UserId' from 23 to another user's id ({{target_id}}) to submit a complaint as another user.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: POST /api/Feedbacks/ (Entry #27) includes 'UserId' and 'rating' in body. Client-controlled UserId allows posting feedback as another user if not validated. Also captcha fields appear client-provided and could be bypassed (sequence/validation).

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Change 'UserId' from 23 to another user's id ({{target_id}}) and supply a rating/comment to create feedback as that user.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: GET /api/Deliverys/{id} & /api/Deliverys (Entries #23, #24) use numeric IDs to fetch delivery info. Presence of listing and specific get-by-id suggests IDOR risk if ownership not enforced.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Change path ID from 1 to another delivery id ({{target_id}}) to attempt access.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: Access to /rest/admin and /rest/admin/* endpoints (Entries #58 and #59) indicates shadow/admin endpoints. They appear accessible with bearer token and return application-configuration resources; presence of admin REST surface on same host suggests potential undocumented functionality (shadow endpoints) usable by attackers.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: No payload change; access admin endpoints directly. Try fetching application configuration or version.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: POST /rest/basket/6/checkout (Entry #63) accepts couponData and paymentId and completes checkout. There is no evidence of server-side verification steps between payment and order creation; client provides paymentId/addressId/deliveryMethodId directly enabling sequence bypass by supplying paymentId without real payment processing.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Change 'orderDetails.paymentId' to a payment id you did not legitimately obtain (e.g., 7 or {{target_id}}) or remove payment step to attempt checkout without payment.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: PUT /rest/wallet/balance (Entry #107) allows updating wallet balance via JSON body with 'balance' and 'paymentId'. Client can set arbitrary balance amounts; if server trusts this request and adjusts balance, it's a critical state manipulation allowing crediting wallet.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Change 'balance' from 555 to a larger amount (e.g., 1000000) and set 'paymentId' to a valid id to attempt to credit wallet.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: PUT /rest/basket/6/coupon/{code} (Entry #65) shows client can attempt to apply coupon via PUT with coupon code path parameter. Although the observed response was 404 for code 6665434535, the endpoint design allows clients to specify coupon codes potentially to manipulate pricing.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Change coupon code in path to a desired code ({{target_id}}) to attempt to apply a coupon to the basket.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: Access to /ftp and /ftp/<filename>.pdf (Entries #53, #54) shows accessible file storage endpoints (ftp path) possibly exposing invoice/order PDFs. These appear as shadow/static endpoints not part of main API surface and may disclose internal order documents.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Request another known file name (e.g., order_{id}.pdf) in /ftp path to retrieve invoices.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: Responses embed JWT tokens in cookies and headers which contain internal fields: user id (23), totpSecret, topSecret, and other internal metadata visible in Entry #3 Authorization token content. This leaks internal identifiers and secrets.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: No mutation required. Inspect Authorization Bearer token or cookie 'token' to decode and view internal claims.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: Many /rest/chatbot endpoints and /rest/image-captcha, /rest/captcha, /rest/memories endpoints (Entries #69-76, #67-68, #81-82, #84-86) expose interactive/debug features (chatbot controls, setname, memories upload) that may be considered shadow or application-internal functions accessible via REST surface.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Invoke chatbot actions directly (e.g., action=setname or query=...) or upload memory image to /rest/memories to exercise hidden features.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: POST /rest/memories (Entry #86) accepts multipart file upload (image) with form field 'image' and associates it with user's memories. The request includes Authorization — but the endpoint accepts file content and may allow arbitrary content uploads impacting application state or storage quota. Client controls content and metadata.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Upload a different/malicious file or change form filename to attempt to store arbitrary content for another user's memory if ownership is not validated.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: GET /rest/basket/{id} (Entry #62, #66) exposes basket data by id in path. Client can fetch basket 6 — direct object reference indicates IDOR risk if id belongs to other user.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Change path id from 6 to another basket id ({{target_id}}) to attempt reading another user's basket.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: POST /rest/deluxe-membership (Entry #80) accepts 'paymentMode' and 'paymentId' in body to purchase membership. If server trusts paymentId as proof of payment, clients can bypass payment by supplying arbitrary paymentId. This is state manipulation/sequence bypass risk.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Change 'paymentId' to an id you did not legitimately obtain (e.g., {{target_id}}) or set 'paymentMode' to 'card' and use a fake paymentId.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: GET /rest/track-order/{trackingId} (Entry #99) reveals order tracking by tracking string. Direct access via tracking identifier might expose order data for arbitrary tracking tokens if not validated to the requester. The tracking identifier appears predictable (b783-...).

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Change tracking id in path to another tracking token ({{target_id}}) to attempt access to other users' order status.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: POST /rest/products/{id}/reviews (Entry #91) allows posting reviews specifying 'author' email in request body. Client can impersonate other users by specifying arbitrary author email or manipulate message content, potentially bypassing author validation.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Change 'author' from dummy@mail.com to another user's email (e.g., victim@mail.com) or craft malicious message.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: Endpoint /assets/public/images/uploads/... (Entries #49-51) serves uploaded files and file names include encoded/unusual characters. This can disclose internal file paths and stored filenames (internal disclosure).

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: No mutation required; enumerate /assets/public/images/uploads/ to list files and discover internal filenames.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: POST /api/Cards/ (Entry #15) accepts fullName, cardNum, expMonth, expYear — card details are sent from client. If the server stores full card numbers without proper tokenization and relies on client-provided cardNum for payment flows, this is a state manipulation/data sensitivity issue.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: POST with a chosen cardNum (e.g., 4111111111111111) and exp values to create card entry.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: GET /api/Users (Entry #41) attempted access (status 0) and POST /api/Users/ (Entry #42) allows user creation. If GET /api/Users can list users without auth or with insufficient filtering, it's an IDOR/ACL issue. Observed POST shows creation with security question payloads; potential to enumerate or create users via API.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Attempt GET /api/Users or enumerate user ids via /api/Users/{id} to access profiles. Create user with chosen email.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: Endpoints under /rest like /rest/saveLoginIp, /rest/continue-code, /rest/2fa, /rest/track-order, /rest/ftp, /rest/admin indicate numerous internal/operational endpoints exposed to clients; these are shadow/internal surfaces (shadow endpoints).

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: No mutation; call these /rest endpoints directly to enumerate functionality.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: PUT /rest/wallet/balance (Entry #107) followed by POST /rest/user/data-export (Entry #102) and other user privileged operations indicates flows where wallet or payment state may be modified then used in other operations. If server does not require completed payment confirmation, client can change balance and immediately perform privileged actions (sequence bypass).

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: First set 'balance' to a high value via PUT /rest/wallet/balance, then invoke an action that spends/exports data relying on wallet balance.
reproduction_guide.curl_command: curl -s -k -X PUT "http://localhost:3000/rest/wallet/balance" -H "Authorization: Bearer {{auth_token}}" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"balance":1000000,"paymentId":7}' && curl -s -k -X POST "http://localhost:3000/rest/user/data-export" -H "Authorization: Bearer {{auth_token}}" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"format":"1"}'

potential_vulnerabilities.description: GET /rest/products/search?q= (Entry #96) and other endpoints return/cache continueCode cookie values (Entry #33, #48, #52 etc). The continueCode likely exposes an internal session continuation token in cookies, which is internal disclosure.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: No mutation required — observe response cookies 'continueCode' to access internal continuation tokens.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: GET /rest/user/change-password?current=dummy&new=dummy&repeat=dummy (Entry #101) performs password change via GET query parameters (sensitive) using Authorization. If the endpoint allows changing other users' passwords by altering auth or parameters, IDOR/ACL issues may exist. Use of GET with credentials in URL may leak internal secrets.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Change query to target another user context (no direct id parameter visible). Attempt to call with someone else's token or tamper tokens.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: GET /rest/whoami (Entry #104) and /rest/user endpoints expose user info. If these endpoints allow retrieving arbitrary user info by swapping tokens or ids, could be IDOR. The traffic shows tokens with user id in claims — server may rely on tokens; potential risk if tokens are forgeable or long-lived.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Call /rest/user or /rest/user/whoami with another token to attempt to access another user's profile; modify Authorization header accordingly.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: POST /api/Addresss/ (Entry #4) allows creating addresses and accepts full payload including country, mobileNum, zipCode, streetAddress, city, state. Client-supplied creation of address with arbitrary values can be used to inject unexpected data (state manipulation).

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: POST a new address with modified fields, or set Address 'country' to another country string.
reproduction_guide.curl_command: curl -s -k -X POST "http://localhost:3000/api/Addresss/" -H "Authorization: Bearer {{auth_token}}" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"country":"Indonesia","fullName":"home","mobileNum":6277711133,"zipCode":"144444","streetAddress":"Jl. Raya","city":"Bandung","state":"Jawa Barat"}'

potential_vulnerabilities.description: Socket.io endpoints (Entries #108-113) include tokens and continueCode in cookies and appear to accept arbitrary messages (Entry #111 shows message payload ["verifyLocalXssChallenge","shirt"]). Websocket interactions may leak or accept internal commands and disclose internal functionality.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Send socket.io messages (e.g., ['verifyLocalXssChallenge','shirt']) over polling or websocket transport with token to test hidden message handlers.
